docs.title: The Secure Research Environment (SRE)
docs.text:
The Secure Research Environment (SRE) is a controlled, virtual platform designed to balance security and research requirements.

The SRE enables trained researchers to store, access, and collaboratively analyse sensitive research data while adhering to security protocols.

Data entering the SRE (ingress) and leaving the SRE (egress) are governed through role-based approvals, with auditing, and monitoring to meet data governance and security requirements.

Use this guide to:

  • Read about how the SRE protects research project data
  • Learn how to get started using SRE and how to perform role-based tasks
  • Find out where to get additional support

docs.title: CeR services acceptable use terms and conditions
docs.text:
By using Centre for eResearch (CeR) services, you agree to:

  • Only use these services for the purpose of undertaking research, commonly in association with a specific research project or programme. Projects that have a commercial component may have to be hosted on a separately licensed service.
  • Undertake security maintenance on specific services where appropriate (e.g. patching on Nectar Cloud Virtual Machines)
  • Work with CeR to review service settings (e.g., virtual machine allocation or storage options) each year, or as required by a particular service, to ensure efficient and sustainable use.
  • Participate in an annual user survey and provide details of research outputs supported by your use of CeR services.
  • Comply with the University's IT Acceptable Use Policy and IT Security Policy.

docs.title: Application
docs.text:
The CeR acceptable use applies to:

  • All members of the University community, whether at the University or elsewhere
  • Services that CeR provides, directly or indirectly through internal partners (e.g., Connect) and external partners (e.g., REANNZ)

docs.title: Eligibility
docs.text: CeR services are available to doctoral students and University staff for the purposes of undertaking research, commonly a specific research project.

docs.title: Suspension or withdrawal of services
docs.text: Service users should expect email correspondence from CeR regarding specific requirements of acceptable use (e.g., service review or need for security maintenance). Failure to abide by these terms and specific requirements may result in a suspension of service followed by a withdrawal of service.

docs.title: Import (ingress) data directly into the SRE
docs.text:
A data custodian can import (ingress) data and files directly into the Secure Research Environment (SRE) without requiring approval from the ingress approver.

  1. Select Data Ingress from the left-hand project menu
  2. Select Choose File to find a file from your computer You can zip up files to upload multiple files at once
  3. Once displayed, select Upload to copy your file to the staging area Review Storage Utilisation from the left-hand project menu, or in the bottom-right of the Project Dashboard, to confirm sufficient free storage space in the staging are and Project Storage.
  4. Select Request Ingress This moves the file(s) from the staging area, and an email is sent to you to confirm your completed ingress request. You will see the new ingress request in Your ingress request history with the request State showing as completed. Note: All files are virus-scanned before being moved from the staging area.

  1. The files will be moved into a timestamped folder within the ingress sub-folder of your Data Custodian storage folder (username-dc). Access this folder from the personal storage area.
    • Windows VM:: Click on the File Explorer from the taskbar at the bottom of the virtual desktop. Select This PC to display available folders within “Network locations”. Select personal > username-dc > ingress.
    • Linux VM: Click on File Manager from the taskbar at the bottom of the virtual desktop. Select personal > username-dc > ingress.

docs.title: File and data management
docs.text:
A Data Custodian can access and manage data and file(s) across the project storage locations to ensure that data and associated files are shared only with appropriate project team members.

Possible project actions include:

  • Store source (raw) project data to the project-ro folder. The content of this folder cannot be edited by other users, but a researcher can make a working copy for analysis. Any shared project data or files that can be modified by all users can be stored in the project-rw folder.
  • Store files that need to be accessed by a specific project member to their project-personal folder, usually named [username]-r.
  • Store files that need to be accessed by a project sub-group to a customised folder, as appropriate.
  • Delete data and files from shared and personal project folders, as appropriate.

A Data Custodian can view data and files within the ingress-approver and egress-approver folders. This enables file storage visibility and allows the Data Custodian to view progress of pending ingress/egress requests.

docs.title: Export (egress) data directly out of the SRE
docs.text:
A Data Custodian can export (egress) data and files directly out of the Secure Research Environment (SRE) without requiring approval from the egress approver.

  1. Open your personal folder username-dc on the Virtual Desktop and copy the file to be downloaded into the egress subfolder. All files in the egress sub-folder will be copied to the staging area when a request is submitted. If you have file(s) from an earlier egress request in this folder, please delete those files before submitting a new request.
  2. Return to Data Egress on the Project Dashboard.
  3. Select Request Egress. The file(s) will be available for download, and you will receive an email confirming your completed egress request. The egress request will be listed in Your egress request history with the request State showing as completed.
  4. Select the file link under Files available for download.
  5. Go to the Downloads folder on your local computer to access the file(s) and move them to a secure storage location (e.g., a project Research Drive).

docs.title: Request for change of user's role/permission level
docs.text: A Data Custodian can request for a specific user’s role to be changed within a project or give them a different permission level (read-write or read-only) in SRE. To request, please send an email to the SRE team.

docs.title: Request to add/remove a user from the project
docs.text: A Data Custodian can request for a specific user to be added or deleted from the project in SRE. Please send an email to the SRE team with the users' details – full name, USERNAME, email and role in SRE (researcher/data custodian/ingress-approver/egress-approver).

docs.title: As a Data Egress Approver
docs.text: As an Egress Approver, use Data Egress Requests to check and approve files(s) that a Researcher wants to export from the project environment.

docs.title: View egress requests
docs.text:
1. You will receive an email informing you of an Egress Request to approve.
  2. Log in to the SRE and, if needed, change to the Egress Approver role.
  3. Select Data Egress Requests from the left-hand project menu on the Project Dashboard.
  1. Use the Management VM to view and inspect the file(s).
    • Windows VM: Click on the File Explorer from the taskbar at the bottom of the virtual desktop. Select This PC to display available folders within "Network locations". Select project_shared > ingress-approver > username-r (user who made the request).
    • Linux VM: Click on the File Manager from the taskbar at the bottom of the virtual desktop. Select project_shared > egress-approver > username-r (user who made the request).

docs.title: Approve or decline a request
docs.text:
1. Return to Data Egress Requests on the Project Dashboard.
  2. Approve or Reject the egress request. The request State in Egress request history will change from pending_approval to completed. The files will be automatically deleted from the staging area following approval or rejection.

Please get in touch with the researcher if the request is rejected and provide them with advice for the next steps.

docs.title: As a Data Ingress Approver
docs.text: As an Ingress Approver, use Data Ingress Requests to check and approve files(s) that a Researcher wants to import into the project environment.

docs.title: View ingress requests
docs.text:
1. You will receive an email informing you of an Ingress Request to approve.
  2. Log in to the SRE and, if needed, change to the Ingress Approver role.
  3. Select Data Ingress Requests from the left-hand project menu on the Project Dashboard.
  1. Use the Management VM to view and inspect the file(s).
    • Windows VM: Click on the File Explorer from the taskbar at the bottom of the virtual desktop. Select This PC to display available folders within "Network locations". Select project_shared > ingress-approver > username-r (user who made the request).
    • Linux VM: Click on the File Manager from the taskbar at the bottom of the virtual desktop. Select project_shared > ingress-approver > username-r (user who made the request).

docs.title: Approve or decline a request
docs.text:
1. Return to Data Ingess Requests on the Project Dashboard.
  2. Approve or Reject the ingress request. The request State in Ingress request history will change from pending_approval to completed. The files will be automatically deleted from the staging area following approval or rejection.

docs.title: Import data (Ingress Request)
docs.text: As a researcher, use the Ingress Request to import files from your computer or a location outside of the Secure Research Environment.

docs.title: Create a new Ingress Request
docs.text:
1. Select Data Ingress from the left-hand project menu
  2. Select Choose File to find a file from your computer You can zip up files to upload multiple files at once
  3. Once displayed, select Upload to copy your file to the staging area Review Storage Utilisation from the left-hand project menu, or in the bottom-right of the Project Dashboard, to confirm sufficient free storage space in the staging area and Project Storage. If you were partway through an Ingress Request and logged out after 15 minutes of inactivity, you will see a file upload failure notification prompting you to log in again.
  1. Select Request Ingress This moves the files into the stagin area. A notificaiton is sent to you and the Ingress Approver to evaluate your request, and you will see the request State in Your Ingress request history change from creating to pending_approval. All files are virus-scanned before being sent to the Ingress Approver for approval.
  2. Wait for the review process to complete.

docs.title: Access files for analysis
docs.text:
1. If the Ingress Request is approved, you will receive an email notification, and the request State in Your Ingress request history will change from pending_approval to completed.
  1. The files will be moved into a timestamped folder within the ingress sub-folder of your personal storage folder (username-r). Access this folder from within the personal storage area. Keep the file in your personal folder or copy/move it into project-rw to share and collaborate with the rest of your team. You can access the project-rw folder within the project-shared storage area.

If the Ingress Approver rejects your request, you will receive an email notification of the rejection, and you can contact the Ingress Approver for clarification. The request is marked as rejected, and the file is deleted from the staging area.

docs.title: Analyse data
docs.text:
Use a virtual desktop to access and work with project data on a secure VM.

  1. Choose Virtual Desktops from the left-hand project menu and select the Research VM (either Windows or Linux, as available).

  1. Access project data from the network folders.
    • Windows VM: Click on the File Explorer from the taskbar at the bottom of the virtual desktop. Select This PC to display available folders within "Network locations" to open the folder you want.
    • Linux VM: Click on the File Manager from the taskbar at the bottom of the virtual desktop. Select personal or project_shared to display available folders. Personal folders, accessed within the personal storage area, are intended for individual use, while folders within the project-shared storage area enable collaboration across the project team.

  1. Select your software from the desktop. If your software is not available on the desktop, click on the Search icon in the taskbar, type in and select the software you need.
  2. Once the analysis is complete, select project-rw or your personal folder (username-r) and press Save to save your output. As a researcher, you cannot save a file in the project-ro folder. Saving your files to the VM's Desktop and Documents folders is not recommended, as VMs are replaceable and the files you save there could be lost.

docs.title: Export data (Egress Request)
docs.text: As a researcher, use the Egress Request to download your data outputs to your local computer or a location outside of the Secure Research Environment.

docs.title: Create a new Egress Request
docs.text:
1. Open your personal folder (username-r) on the virtual desktop and copy the file to be downloaded into the egress subfolder.
  1. Return to Data Egress from the left-hand project menu on the Project Dashboard.
  2. Select Request Egress This will copy any files from your egress sub-folder into the staging area (egress-approver folder) where an Egress Approver can review the files to ensure there are no identifiable or sensitive information. An email is sent to you and the Egress Approver to evaluate your request, and you will see the request State in Your egress request history change from creating to pending-approval.
  3. Wait for the review process to complete.

docs.title: Access files for download
docs.text:
1. If the Egress Request is approved, you will receive an email notification, and the request State in Your egress request history will change from pending-approval to completed.
  2. The files will be available for download. Click on the zip file under the Files available for download
  3. Go to your local computer's Download folder. Unzip the downloaded folder - with file(s) inside - and save to an appropriate location.

If the request is rejected, contact the Egress Approver for further details.

docs.title: Data Storage
docs.text:
Each SRE project includes a set of default storage locations to support secure data management, collaboration and controlled data transfer (ingress and egress). Additional folders and customised folder structures can be configured during project onboarding.

Storage is divided into personal and project-shared areas. Personal folders are intended for individual use, while project-shared folders enable collaboration across the project team.

The table below provides an overview of the default storage folders available within each project.

Folder name Access Who can Access Purpose Notes project-personal (username-r) Read/Write (own folder) Individual researcher (Data Custodian has full access) Private working space for individual research users Contains ingress and egress subfolders data-custodian (username-dc) Read/Write Data Custodians Used for direct data ingress/egress and data management Contains ingress and egress subfolders project-rw Read/Write All project users Shared working directory for collaboration Files can be edited by all users project-ro Read-only All project users (Data Custodian has full access) Stores raw or source data User must copy files out before editing ingress-approver Read/Review Ingress Approvers (Data Custodian can view) Temporary storage for files awaiting ingress approval Files are removed after approval or rejection egress-approver Read/Review Egress Approvers (Data Custodian can view) Temporary storage for files awaiting egress approval Files are removed after approval or rejection

Warning: Data saved outside these folders (e.g., on the VM Desktop or Documents folders) are not persistent and may be lost.

The data will only reside in the SRE during the research project. After project completion, a cost-effective, secure approach to data should be used (e.g., data should be securely archived or deleted).

docs.title: Definition of common terms used in SRE
docs.text:
Username - Your username/login (e.g., jsmi123)

Data ingress – Data (files or folders) which are brought into SRE from outside. These are done through requests and the person who vets these requests is called an Ingress Approver.

Data egress - Data (files or folders) which are taken out of the SRE. These are also done through requests and the person who vets these requests is called an Egress Approver.

Virtual desktop - A virtual desktop is a software computing platform with apps, tools and data that is accessible from multiple devices and locations over a network.

Airlock – An intermediate secure area where data resides waiting to be vetted before it moves in or out of the SRE.

VPN - Virtual Private Network establish a secure connection from outside the University to our network. This means the data passing between your computer and the University network is protected, as it is strongly encrypted. For more info, go to uoa-vpn-service

Read-write permission - Grants the user ability to view and modify a file includes creating files, deleting files, and renaming files.

Read-only permissions - Grants the user ability only to view and read a file.

MFA - Multi-factor authentication, or MFA, is a security process that helps verify users' identities before letting them access networks or online applications.

Authy – Authy is an app used to generate the time-dependent six-digit code needed for access to University online services. The prompt for the code will appear after the username and password screen of the University online service you are trying to access. When the prompt appears, open Authy on your mobile device and enter the code that appears. For more info, please check out two-factor-authentication-authy

docs.title: Pre-requisites
docs.text:
Ensure you have the following SRE access requirements:

  • University of Auckland username and password
  • VPN access (required off-campus or outside the University of Auckland intranet)
  • Internet connection and computer
  • Supported web browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox)
  • Multi-factor authentication

docs.title: Logging into the SRE
docs.text:
You can access the SRE by clicking here or entering the following URL:

https://www.sre.auckland.ac.nz/

To log in:

  1. Sign in with your University of Auckland username and password
  2. Enter your Two-Factor Authentication code
  3. Once logged in, you will be directed to one of the following pages:
    • The dashboard of your project, if you are a member of exactly one project.
    • A page where you can choose a project, if you are member of more than one project.

docs.title: Choosing your project
docs.text:
You will only be asked to choose a project if you are a member of more than one project.

The main elements of this page are shown below.

  1. Displays the username of the logged in user
  2. Log out of the SRE
  3. Project selection drop-down menu. All projects you have access to will be displayed in this drop-down.
  4. SRE information page
  5. Privacy policy
  6. SRE user guide

docs.title: Project Dashboard
docs.text:
The main elements of the project dashboard are shown below.

  1. Click on Secure Research Environment to switch projects (returns you to the SRE landing page)
  2. Displays the name of the open project
  3. Use the left-hand navigation to toggle between SRE activities, depending on your project role
  4. Minimise the left-hand project menu
  5. Displays the logged-in account and current project role If you have more than one project role, you can switch between roles by selecting an option from this drop-down menu.
  6. Log out of the SRE
  7. Project storage utilisation (quick view) Select Storage Utilisation from the left-hand project menu to display full storage use and quota information.

docs.title: Scheduled Maintenance
docs.text:
The SRE undergoes scheduled maintenance on the first Tuesday of every month.

During this time, the environment will be in maintenance mode for the full day and may be unavailable.

Any other SRE maintenance actions outside of these windows will be announced by an outage message on the web portal.

docs.title: Security and access controls
docs.text:
The SRE is hosted on premises. Each project environment is configured to provide the infrastructure, software and tools required to work collaboratively on sensitive research data. Secure virtual desktops enable researchers to work with sensitive data while maintaining greater control and protection. Data is stored separately for each research project and can only be accessed by the team assigned to that environment.

The SRE has enhanced security features to protect project data and is designed to enable data governance within projects using role-based responsibilities and access controls.

docs.title: Multi-tiered security
docs.text:
• Aligned with University security standards
  • Project data is encrypted
  • Auditable data import (ingress), access and export (egress)
  • Each project environment is isolated from each other, as well as from the internet and other University systems, except where needed (e.g., to provide access or to maintain security updates). SRE users cannot access the internet (unless approved), copy/paste or drag and drop into or out of the project environment, or mount a USB or local drive.
  • Enhanced session security to protect project data.
    • You will be logged out of the project environment after 15 mins of inactivity
    • The VM connection will be closed after 10 minutes of inactivity
    • If you have been logged out, you will be prompted to log in and enter two-factor authentication again to continue.

docs.title: Access controls
docs.text:
• Secure web portal access via web browser
  • Access requires two-factor authentication for authorised project team members
  • Role-based controlled access and rights based on project needs Each role can be held by one or more project team members. A project team member can hold more than one role.

The following table summarises the responsibilities for each project role in the SRE.

Role Ingress Egress VM Access Manage Users Data Custodian Direct Direct ✓ ✓ Researcher Request Request ✓ ✕ Ingress Approver Approve ✕ ✓ ✕ Egress Approver ✕ Approve ✓ ✕

docs.title: Getting Help
docs.text:
If you have any questions about the SRE service, or require assistance with an existing SRE project, please email researchdata@auckland.ac.nz.

Please include the following information:
  • Project name
  • Role
  • Time of issue
  • Screenshot

docs.title: Virtual desktops
docs.text: A virtual desktop (or virtual machine, VM) is a virtual version of a computer that can be accessed from multiple devices and locations through a web browser. It is pre-installed with software, tools and data to enable secure data analysis.

docs.title: Standard options
docs.text:
• Each project environment has a Management VM and one or more Research VMs.
  • VMs can have Microsoft Windows Server or Linux Operating Systems.
  • A list of standard software available within the project environment can be found on the SRE page of Research Resources. Other applications may be installed by the SRE team upon request, subject to licensing restrictions.
